title: Rate controller islanding, preemptive shedding, and state recovery playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In multi-region deployments, the rate-controller fabric can become isolated (islanding) due to networking flaps, partial control-plane failures, or regional traffic spikes. Islanded controllers risk either over-admitting requests (if they believe global credits exist) or over-shedding (if they become overly conservative), both causing SLO violations. This ticket designs a playbook to: 1) detect early islanding and preemptively shed non-SLA traffic, 2) preserve fairness across tenant classes while minimizing tail latency impact, and 3) enable fast, safe state recovery and reconciliation once control connectivity is restored.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller instances can detect islanding within 15s using heartbeat and lease heuristics and emit a standardized event.
2) A preemptive-shedding policy is applied automatically that reduces non-SLA allocations by >=70% within 30s of detection.
3) Controllers persist compact checksumed token-state snapshots to durable store at most every 60s and can rehydrate into a consistent degraded admission state within 45s after reconnection.
4) Dashboards show SLO impact projections for any controller islanding event and automated alerts trigger at projected SLO breach probability > 5%.
5) Chaos tests (simulated partial-control-plane outages) run in staging and demonstrate <1% of requests are routed to emergency-restore slow-path during reconcilation window for typical tenant mix.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Use lease-based local credits to allow controllers to make safe admission decisions when disconnected. Tradeoff: brief divergence vs blocking; chosen for availability.
- Preemptive shedding is tier-aware: reserve a conservative baseline for premium tenants and aggressively shed best-effort traffic. Tradeoff: potential temporary unfairness for bursty paid tenants vs protecting SLOs.
- Keep snapshots compact (per-tenant aggregate credits + vector clock) to avoid high write amplification. Tradeoff: less granular reconstruction but faster rehydration.
- Avoid synchronous global consensus during failover to limit latency; rely on eventual reconciliation with deterministic merge rules.
implementation_plan:
1) Add islanding detector to controller agent: heartbeat, lease counters, and transport-level circuit hints (2 weeks).
2) Implement tiered preemptive-shedding policy module with configurable knobs (preserve_min_reserve_pct, non_sla_shed_pct, emergency_blacklist) (1.5 weeks).
3) Snapshotter: per-controller compact state write to regional durable store (S3/etcd depending on deployment) with checksum and vector clock (1 week).
4) Rehydration worker: deterministic merge rules, safety checks, and safe-mode admission until reconciliation completes (1 week).
5) Observability: dashboards, alerting rules, and synthetic SLO projection job (1 week).
6) Staging chaos engineering and load-testing (2 weeks).
7) Canary rollout to a small set of customers / routes with SLA guardrails (2 weeks).
testing_and_chaos_plan:
- Unit tests for detector, snapshot/rehydration logic, and merge determinism.
- Integration tests simulating network partitions and delayed rehydration with deterministic assertions on admitted counts.
- Load tests with synthetic tenant mix (premium:10%, standard:50%, best-effort:40%) to validate shed percentages and tail latency.
- Chaos scenarios: control-plane partition, partial region outage, delayed durable-store writes, flapping reconnection.
- Postmortem checklist for any SLO breach during staging runs.
observability_and_alerting:
- Metrics: islanding_detected_count, islanding_duration_seconds, preemptive_shed_rate_by_tier, rehydration_time_seconds, admitted_tokens_delta.
- Dashboards: real-time islanding map, tenant impact heatmap, SLO projection panel that simulates how current islanding affects 1m/5m error/latency SLOs.
- Alerts: P1 when projected SLO breach probability > 5% or islanding duration > 60s for high-traffic regions.
- Runbook link (staging+prod) in related_docs.
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Overly aggressive shedding harms revenue-critical tenants. Mitigation: conservative reserves and manual override; canary with premium-only traffic pinned to non-degraded controllers.
- Risk: Snapshot store delay causing stale rehydration. Mitigation: include local transient leases and conservative admissions while snapshot age > threshold.
- Risk: Deterministic merge rule bugs leading to double-admit. Mitigation: strong invariants in tests and a temporary global contestability lock during first rollouts.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: feature flags and internal-only off-by-default rollout. Phase 1: enable detector and observability only. Phase 2: enable preemptive shedding in staging and run chaos. Phase 3: canary on low-risk customers and selected regions. Phase 4: gradual ramp with telemetry SLO checkpoints and automatic rollback on breach.
Manual rollback: disable shedding policy and re-enable global conservative mode.
updates: 2025-10-13: Initial design doc drafted and reviewed with Reliability. Decided on lease-based local credits as baseline. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RL/Rate+Controller+Islanding+Playbook
2025-10-20: Prototype of islanding detector merged to feature branch. Basic heartbeat + lease counters implemented. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4892
2025-10-27: Implemented compact snapshot format (per-tenant aggregates + vector clock). Added checksum and TTL. Integration tests for snapshot writes passing in CI.

2025-11-01: Preemptive-shedding module merged behind feature flag. Staging load test shows non-SLA shed rate ~72% under partition scenario; premium reserve maintained. Noted increased 95th p99 for standard tier by ~12ms under high spike.
2025-11-02: Observability panels merged. Alert thresholds tuned. Preparing chaos scenarios for next staging run.
